record.title: Preprint reports predictable failures in rarity- and relevance-based memory for LLM group decisions
record.summary: The arXiv preprint introduces CrossProfile, a diagnostic with 60 main templates and 480 ownership variants that keeps fact wording fixed while varying which agents hold supporting, decoy and irrelevant information. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and exploratory hosted DeepSeek runs, the authors report that rarity-first and relevance-first memory heuristics can reverse performance depending on who holds decoy evidence. In the classic hidden-profile condition, relevance-first selection lowers accuracy by about 20–22 points for the two local models, and removing or randomizing holder-attribution tags raises accuracy by about 13–14 points. The study uses constructed tasks and a mechanically defined answer key; it does not estimate failure rates in deployed teams.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors submitted arXiv:2610.37624v1 on 27 October 2026, presenting CrossProfile, a diagnostic of how LLM group-decision memory policies select evidence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports that CrossProfile uses 60 main templates, each with eight ownership variants (480 tasks), holding fact wording and roles fixed while crossing which agents hold support, decoy and irrelevant facts. Its mechanically checked answer key reflects a fixed additive scoring rule that is not stated in the model-facing prompt.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, the authors report that rarity-first selection is approximately tied with random selection when averaged across ownership variants, while their relative performance reverses sharply depending on whether supporting or decoy facts are private versus shared.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the classic condition with private support, shared decoys and private irrelevant facts, relevance-first selection lowers reported accuracy versus rarity-first by 22.2 points for Qwen and 20.0 points for Llama; an oracle relevance filter also loses 23.3 and 31.1 points, respectively. These are results on constructed tasks, not deployed decision outcomes.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the classic constructed condition, the authors report that removing or randomly reassigning contributor-attribution tags while holding line order fixed raises accuracy by roughly 13–14 points on Qwen and Llama. This supports sensitivity to social-proof cues in this prompt setup, not a general claim about real groups.

evidence_gaps.description: The CrossProfile effects and model outputs are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
The mechanically defined answer key is not an external measure of real group decision quality, and transfer to naturally occurring deliberation is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported ownership and attribution effects generalize, memory selection policies could materially affect reliability of multi-agent decisions. This is notable for research and system design, but the current evidence comes from a constructed diagnostic and four tested model variants, not deployed teams.
limitations: The benchmark consists of constructed tasks with mechanically derived keys; the prompt does not state the additive scoring rule, so accuracy measures agreement with the constructed key rather than externally adjudicated decision quality.
Only four model variants are evaluated; DeepSeek-Pro uses 30 templates, and hosted-model runs are described as exploratory.
Ownership changes when a fact first appears, contributor tags and token cost as well as selection priority; the paper adds controls, but transfer to natural team discussion remains uncertain.
No independent reproduction, external answer-key validation, real-world team study or deployed failure rate was established.

brief.summary: The arXiv preprint introduces CrossProfile, a diagnostic with 60 main templates and 480 ownership variants that keeps fact wording fixed while varying which agents hold supporting, decoy and irrelevant information. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and exploratory hosted DeepSeek runs, the authors report that rarity-first and relevance-first memory heuristics can reverse performance depending on who holds decoy evidence. In the classic hidden-profile condition, relevance-first selection lowers accuracy by about 20–22 points for the two local models, and removing or randomizing holder-attribution tags raises accuracy by about 13–14 points. The study uses constructed tasks and a mechanically defined answer key; it does not estimate failure rates in deployed teams.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report ownership-dependent reversals for rarity-first selection, relevance-first losses in the classic hidden-profile cell, and 13–14 point gains in local models when holder-attribution tags are removed or randomized.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public v1 paper specifies a diagnostic design with mechanically checked answer keys and reports its analysis. the research desk did not run the experiment or independently verify the task generator, model outputs or scoring outcomes.
technical.implementation_status: Preprint and constructed benchmark; no deployed-team implementation or field evaluation is established.
technical.mechanism: CrossProfile crosses ownership of support, decoy and irrelevant facts while holding fact text and decision roles fixed. It compares first-mention, rarest-first, relevance-tiered, evidence-summary, random, all-facts and empty memories at token budgets. Contributor tags and line-order controls probe whether the decision model gives social-proof weight to claims repeated by more agents.
technical.novelty: A crossed diagnostic separates evidence rarity from decision usefulness and reveals that a memory heuristic’s direction can depend on which group members hold supporting versus decoy facts.
technical.regime: 60 main CrossProfile templates in 12 decision domains; eight ownership variants per template (480 tasks), four agents, three options and 12 facts each. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct use three seeds; hosted DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash covers all templates and DeepSeek-V4-Pro covers 30 templates as exploratory runs. A separate 65-task HiddenBench analysis is also reported.
technical.reproducibility: The full arXiv HTML describes prompts, metrics, controls and bootstrap procedure. No independent execution or external replication was performed in this activation; no code or dataset artifact was inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: Random-order selection for average policy performance and first-mention selection for ownership-reversal contrasts; all-facts and empty memories are additional controls.

brief.title: Preprint reports predictable failures in rarity- and relevance-based memory for LLM group decisions
brief.why_it_matters: If independently reproduced beyond this constructed benchmark, memory selection and attribution cues could change how multi-agent teams preserve and weigh evidence. The paper shows why average accuracy can conceal large ownership-dependent failures, while its synthetic task key and narrow model regime limit transfer.
